claim: The oligomeric state of plasma membrane proteins is an important determinant of their function.
source: The oligomeric state of plasma membrane proteins is the result of the interactions between individual subunits and an important determinant of their function.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Most approaches to determine oligomeric states rely on extracting protein complexes from their native environment, which may disrupt weaker interactions.
source: Most approaches used to address this question rely on extracting these complexes from their native environment, which may disrupt weaker interactions.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of existing methods in the abstract.

claim: Classical light microscopy suffers from insufficient resolution for determining oligomeric states.
source: Classical light microscopy suffers from insufficient resolution, but super-resolution methods such as single molecule localization microscopy (SMLM) can circumvent this problem.
evidence: This is stated as a known limitation in the abstract.

claim: Super-resolution methods such as SMLM can circumvent the resolution problem of classical light microscopy.
source: Classical light microscopy suffers from insufficient resolution, but super-resolution methods such as single molecule localization microscopy (SMLM) can circumvent this problem.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of SMLM in the abstract.

claim: Traditional SMLM counting strategies require low background noise, high recall rate for fluorescent tags, and intensive post-imaging data processing.
source: This strategy requires low background noise, a high recall rate for the fluorescent tag and intensive post-imaging data processing.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of existing SMLM methods in the abstract.

claim: The dual-color colocalization (DCC) approach allows for accurate in situ counting even with low efficiencies of fluorescent protein detection.
source: Our dual-color colocalization (DCC) approach allows for accurate in situ counting even with low efficiencies of fluorescent protein detection.
evidence: This is stated as a key advantage of the developed method in the abstract.

claim: DCC-SMLM is robust in the presence of background signals.
source: In addition, it is robust in the presence of background signals and does not require temporal clustering of localizations from individual proteins within the same diffraction-limited volume, which greatly simplifies data acquisition and processing.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of the method in the abstract.

claim: DCC-SMLM does not require temporal clustering of localizations from individual proteins within the same diffraction-limited volume.
source: In addition, it is robust in the presence of background signals and does not require temporal clustering of localizations from individual proteins within the same diffraction-limited volume, which greatly simplifies data acquisition and processing.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of the method in the abstract.

claim: The oligomeric state of SLC26 multifunctional anion exchangers has been controversial.
source: We used DCC-SMLM to resolve the controversy surrounding the oligomeric state of two SLC26 multifunctional anion exchangers
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: Most membrane proteins form oligomeric assemblies in which individual subunits cooperate to fulfill specialized functions.
source: Most membrane proteins form oligomeric assemblies, in which individual subunits cooperate to fulfill specialized functions.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: The number of subunits within protein structures is a crucial determinant of their function.
source: The number of subunits within such protein structures is a crucial determinant of their function (Lussier et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lussier et al., 2019.

claim: Native gel electrophoresis has been successfully used to determine oligomeric states of proteins.
source: Native gel electrophoresis has been successfully used to determine oligomeric states of proteins and the molecular determinants of oligomeric assemblies (Detro-Dassen et al., 2008; Gendreau et al., 2004; Schägger and von Jagow, 1991).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: Native gel electrophoresis relies on isolating protein complexes from their native environment, which can disrupt some protein interactions.
source: However, this technique relies on isolating protein complexes from their native environment, which can disrupt some protein interactions.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of native gel electrophoresis in the introduction.

claim: In situ methods such as fluorescence correlation spectroscopy, stepwise photobleaching, and SMLM have become increasingly popular for determining oligomeric states.
source: To overcome this limitation, in situ methods such as fluorescence correlation spectroscopy (Chen et al., 2003), stepwise photobleaching (Ulbrich and Isacoff, 2007), and single molecule localization microscopy (SMLM) (Annibale et al., 2011; Sengupta et al., 2011) have become increasingly popular in recent years.
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: Stepwise photobleaching relies on the irreversible and stochastic photobleaching of fluorescent tags linked to the subunit to be counted.
source: Stepwise photobleaching relies on the irreversible and stochastic photobleaching of fluorescent tags linked to the subunit to be counted, and the resulting intensity steps depend on the number of subunits within the complex being tested.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the stepwise photobleaching method in the introduction.

claim: Stepwise photobleaching is only feasible for low expression densities as it is limited by the resolution of light microscopy.
source: However, this approach is only feasible for low expression densities as it is limited by the resolution of light microscopy.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of stepwise photobleaching in the introduction.

claim: Xenopus laevis oocytes are most often used for stepwise photobleaching because they are large in diameter and ectopic protein expression can be controlled by adjusting the amount of injected RNA.
source: Therefore, Xenopus laevis oocytes, which are large in diameter and in which ectopic protein expression can be controlled by adjusting the amount of injected RNA, are most often used for this method (Ulbrich and Isacoff, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Ulbrich and Isacoff, 2007.

claim: Some proteins exhibit a different oligomeric state when expressed in the Xenopus system compared with mammalian expression systems.
source: However, some proteins exhibit a different oligomeric state when expressed in the Xenopus system compared with mammalian expression systems (Krashia et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Krashia et al., 2010.

claim: For mammalian cells, the resolution limit of light microscopy can be circumvented using super-resolution microscopy methods.
source: For mammalian cells, the resolution limit of light microscopy can be circumvented using super-resolution microscopy methods (Durisic et al., 2014; Hummer et al., 2016; Lee et al., 2012; Nan et al., 2013; Nicovich et al., 2017; Puchner et al., 2013; Sengupta et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: SMLM increases resolution by reconstructing the precise positions of isolated fluorophore emissions detected over thousands of frames.
source: SMLM increases resolution by reconstructing the precise positions of isolated fluorophore emissions detected over thousands of frames (Betzig et al., 2006; Rust et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Betzig et al., 2006 and Rust et al., 2006.

claim: The fluorophores used for quantitative SMLM are usually photoactivatable or photoconvertible fluorescent proteins that are activated or converted at wavelengths different from that of the excitation laser.
source: The fluorophores used for quantitative SMLM are usually photoactivatable or photoconvertible fluorescent proteins that are activated or converted at wavelengths different from that of the excitation laser (Li and Vaughan, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Li and Vaughan, 2018.

claim: To increase the resolution in SMLM, the simultaneous activation of multiple fluorophores within the same diffraction-limited volume must be avoided.
source: To increase the resolution in SMLM, the simultaneous activation of multiple fluorophores within the same diffraction-limited volume must be avoided.
evidence: This is stated as a requirement for SMLM in the introduction.

claim: During long SMLM recordings, inherent mechanical and thermal fluctuations, as well as sample drift, combine to reduce spatial resolution.
source: During the long recordings required for SMLM, inherent mechanical and thermal fluctuations, as well as the sample drift, combine to reduce spatial resolution.
evidence: This is stated as a challenge in SMLM in the introduction.

claim: The complex photophysics of fluorescent protein blinking may result in over- or undercounting.
source: The complex photophysics of fluorescent protein blinking may additionally result in over- or undercounting (Annibale et al., 2011; Lee et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Annibale et al., 2011 and Lee et al., 2012.

claim: Background noise cannot be easily distinguished from genuine signals at the single molecule level.
source: Another source of miscounting is the background noise, which cannot be easily distinguished from genuine signals at the single molecule level (Shivanandan et al., 2014; Zhao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Shivanandan et al., 2014 and Zhao et al., 2018.

claim: It is impossible to detect all fluorophores in the sample because the probability of having a fluorescent marker detected during the imaging period (the recall rate) is always less than one.
source: Furthermore, it is impossible to detect all fluorophores in the sample because the probability of having a fluorescent marker detected during the imaging period (i.e., the recall rate) is always less than one.
evidence: This is stated as a fundamental limitation in the introduction.

claim: Low recall rates likely arise from a combination of incomplete protein translation or misfolding, failure to get activated or converted, and pre-imaging bleaching.
source: This likely arises from a combination of incomplete protein translation or misfolding, failure to get activated or converted, and pre-imaging bleaching (Durisic et al., 2014; Nicovich et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Durisic et al., 2014 and Nicovich et al., 2017.

claim: The binomial strategy demands a recall rate of about 0.5 or higher to ensure reasonable resolution between different oligomeric states.
source: This binomial strategy demands a recall rate of about 0.5or higher to ensure reasonable resolution between different oligomeric states (Durisic et al., 2014; Ulbrich and Isacoff, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Durisic et al., 2014 and Ulbrich and Isacoff, 2007.

claim: The human SLC26 family has 10 members that function as anion transporters or channels as well as the motor protein in cochlear outer hair cells.
source: The human SLC26 family has 10 members that function as anion transporters or channels as well as the motor protein in cochlear outer hair cells.
evidence: This is stated as background information in the introduction.

claim: Naturally occurring mutations in SLC26 proteins are associated with growth defects, chronic diarrhea or deafness.
source: The physiological importance of these proteins is illustrated by the growth defects, chronic diarrhea or deafness associated with naturally occurring mutations.
evidence: This is stated as background information in the introduction.

claim: Biochemical and recent structural studies indicated that SLC26 proteins exist as dimers.
source: Biochemical and recent structural studies indicated that the proteins exist as dimers (Detro-Dassen et al., 2008; Geertsma et al., 2015; Walter et al., 2019)
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: Other studies have proposed a tetrameric state for SLC26 proteins.
source: whereas other studies have proposed a tetrameric state (Hallworth and Nichols, 2012; Sinha et al., 2010; Zheng et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: The SLC17 family includes proton-driven vesicular glutamate, aspartate, sialic acid, and nucleotide transporters, as well as Na+-coupled phosphate transporters.
source: The SLC17 family includes proton-driven vesicular glutamate, aspartate, sialic acid, and nucleotide transporters, as well as Na+-coupled phosphate transporters.
evidence: This is stated as background information in the introduction.

claim: Direct determination of Pd from single-color microscopy images is impossible, as the total number of proteins, including those not exhibiting fluorescence, is unknown.
source: However, direct determination of Pd from single-color microscopy images is impossible, as the total number of proteins, including those not exhibiting fluorescence, is unknown.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation in the Results section.

claim: mVenus was chosen as the fluorescent marker protein M because of the very low background signal in its detection channel.
source: We chose mVenus (Nagai et al., 2002) as the fluorescent marker protein M because of the very low background signal in its detection channel (Figure 1D–E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1D-E.

claim: mVenus is derived from yellow fluorescent protein with several improvements such as faster maturation, a monomeric structure, and high tolerance to cellular acidification, and the halide concentration.
source: mVenus is derived from yellow fluorescent protein with several improvements such as faster maturation, a monomeric structure, and high tolerance to cellular acidification, and the halide concentration (Nagai et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Nagai et al., 2002.

claim: mVenus blinks by cycling between fluorescent and dark states under continuous illumination with the excitation laser.
source: Like other GFP derivatives, it blinks by cycling between fluorescent and dark states under continuous illumination with the excitation laser (Dickson et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Dickson et al., 1997.

claim: PAmCherry was chosen as the indicator because it is quickly bleached by continuous excitation after activation.
source: PAmCherry was chosen as the indicator because it is quickly bleached by continuous excitation after activation (Durisic et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Durisic et al., 2014.

claim: The PAmCherry channel had considerably more background signals than the mVenus channel.
source: However, this channel had considerably more background signals.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1D-E.

claim: Drift correction reduced the radius of clustered signals to ~30 nm.
source: This correction reduced the radius of clustered signals to ~30 nm (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: Lateral chromatic aberration (LCA) can be described as a set of linear functions centered on the optical axis of the microscope.
source: We confirmed earlier reports that lateral chromatic aberration (LCA) can be described as a set of linear functions centered on the optical axis of the microscope (Erdelyi et al., 2013; Kozubek and Matula, 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Erdelyi et al., 2013 and Kozubek and Matula, 2000.

claim: LCA could be reduced to 13.8±8.9 nm for bead samples using linear fit correction.
source: This way the LCA could be reduced to 13.8±8.9 nm for bead samples (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2D and E.

claim: The axial chromatic aberration (ACA) was less than 100 nm and thus considered negligible for SMLM signal registration in only two dimensions.
source: The axial chromatic aberration (ACA) determined as the focus offset between colors was less than 100 nm and thus considered negligible for SMLM signal registration in only two dimensions (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Following correction of chromatic aberrations, highest densities of red clusters were found within a radius of ~100 nm around mVenus clusters for both barttin and Kir2.1.
source: Following correction, highest densities of red clusters were found within a radius of ~100 nm around mVenus clusters for both proteins, representing the achievable two-color resolution of our experimental setup.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2H.

claim: 100 nm was chosen as the threshold distance for colocalization.
source: We therefore chose 100 nm as the threshold distance for colocalization.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the RDF analysis.

claim: A large proportion of membrane proteins remain mobile after fixation with paraformaldehyde (PFA) alone, requiring the addition of glutaraldehyde (GA) or the use of cold methanol (MeOH) for adequate immobilization.
source: A large proportion of membrane proteins remain mobile after fixation with paraformaldehyde (PFA) alone, requiring the addition of glutaraldehyde (GA) or the use of cold methanol (MeOH) for adequate immobilization (Stanly et al., 2016; Tanaka et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Stanly et al., 2016 and Tanaka et al., 2010.

claim: Both MeOH and aldehyde fixation methods led to comparable correlation distances between the two colors.
source: Both fixation methods led to comparable correlation distances between the two colors (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: Upon MeOH fixation, a significantly higher signal density, a higher ratio of PAmCherry clusters to mVenus clusters and a higher colocalization ratio were observed compared with aldehyde fixation.
source: However, upon MeOH fixation we observed a significantly higher signal density, a higher ratio of PAmCherry clusters to mVenus clusters and a higher colocalization ratio than with the aldehyde fixation (Figure 3A', B' and C–F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Fixation with cold methanol better preserved the function of the fluorescent proteins compared with PFA/GA fixation.
source: Therefore, we concluded that fixation with cold methanol better preserved the function of the fluorescent proteins compared with PFA/GA fixation and, therefore, we chose cold methanol as our routine fixation reagent.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Results section based on the comparison data.

claim: The fusion pattern of PAmCherry and mVenus affected the colocalization ratio.
source: The results, as shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1, indicated that the fusion pattern did affect the colocalization ratio.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Barttin is a monomeric protein.
source: the monomeric ClC-K chloride channel β-subunit barttin (Scholl et al., 2006; Estévez et al., 2001)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Scholl et al., 2006 and Estévez et al., 2001.

claim: ClC-2 and ClC-K are dimeric chloride channels.
source: the dimeric chloride channels ClC-2 and ClC-K (Park et al., 2017; Stölting et al., 2014; Thiemann et al., 1992)
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: EAAT2 is a trimeric glutamate transporter.
source: the trimeric glutamate transporter EAAT2 (Canul-Tec et al., 2017; Nothmann et al., 2011)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Canul-Tec et al., 2017 and Nothmann et al., 2011.

claim: Kir2.1 (Kcnj2) is a tetrameric potassium channel.
source: the tetrameric potassium channel Kir2.1 (Kcnj2, Doyle et al., 1998)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Doyle et al., 1998.

claim: hrCNE results confirmed the reported oligomeric states of the calibration proteins and demonstrated that the two linked fluorescent proteins did not interfere with the reported quaternary structure.
source: Our results also demonstrate that the two linked fluorescent proteins did not interfere with the reported quaternary structure.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: A global fit of bootstrap resampled experimental data from all five proteins with known oligomeric states to Equation 1 suggested a low recall rate (p) of 0.12 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.12–0.13) for PAmCherry.
source: A global fit of bootstrap resampled (10,000 resamples) experimental data from all five proteins with known oligomeric states to Equation 1 suggested a low recall rate (p) of 0.12 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.12–0.13) for PAmCherry.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on fitting analysis.

claim: Fitting to Equation 4 gave values of 0.30 (95% CI: 0.21–0.39) for m and 0.17 (95% CI: 0.15–0.18) for p.
source: Fitting to Equation 4 gave values of 0.30 (95% CI: 0.21–0.39) for m and 0.17 (95% CI: 0.15–0.18) for p.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on fitting analysis.

claim: The model with modification factor m (Equation 4) aligns better with the data compared to the simpler model (Equations 1–3), especially for the monomeric reference protein.
source: As expected, this model only aligns slightly better with the data (R2 = 0.97) compared to the simpler model (Equations 1–3). However, the improvement is especially visible for the monomeric reference protein (Figure 4A)
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: M2 values reached their lowest values for a dimeric state of SLC26 proteins.
source: As shown in Figure 4C-H, M2 values reached their lowest values for a dimeric state of SLC26 proteins
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 4C-H.

claim: M2 values reached their lowest values for a monomeric state of all SLC17 proteins.
source: As shown in Figure 4C-H, M2 values reached their lowest values for a dimeric state of SLC26 proteins and for a monomeric state of all SLC17 proteins.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 4C-H.

claim: The two-sample K.-S. test confirmed that SLC26A3 is most likely a dimeric protein.
source: With this test, we confirmed the results of the M2 values and also demonstrated that SLC26A3 is most likely a dimeric protein as it showed a significantly different distribution compared to reference proteins with other oligomeric states (Figure 4I).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 4I.

claim: hrCNE independently confirmed the oligomeric states of SLC26 and SLC17 proteins determined by DCC-SMLM.
source: Moreover, we independently confirmed our results for the oligomeric states of SLC26 and SLC17 proteins with hrCNE utilizing the same constructs and expression system as in our DCC-SMLM experiments (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: DCC-SMLM established a dimeric state for the epithelial anion exchanger SLC26A3.
source: Using mVenus as the marker fluorescent protein and PAmCherry as the indicator fluorescent protein for counting, we established a dimeric state for two representatives of the SLC26 family, the epithelial anion exchanger SLC26A3
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the experimental results.

claim: DCC-SMLM established a dimeric state for the motor protein prestin (Slc26a5).
source: Using mVenus as the marker fluorescent protein and PAmCherry as the indicator fluorescent protein for counting, we established a dimeric state for two representatives of the SLC26 family, the epithelial anion exchanger SLC26A3 and the motor protein prestin (Slc26a5)
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the experimental results.

claim: DCC-SMLM established a monomeric state for vGlut1, -2, and -3.
source: and a monomeric state for four representatives of the SLC17 family, the vesicular glutamate transporters vGlut1, -2, and -3
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the experimental results.

claim: DCC-SMLM established a monomeric state for the lysosomal sialic acid transporter sialin.
source: and a monomeric state for four representatives of the SLC17 family, the vesicular glutamate transporters vGlut1, -2, and -3 and the lysosomal sialic acid transporter sialin.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the experimental results.

claim: DCC-SMLM overcomes several limitations of methods commonly used to determine the oligomeric state of proteins.
source: Our DCC-SMLM approach (Figure 4—figure supplement 3) overcomes several limitations of the methods commonly used to determine the oligomeric state of proteins.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Unlike biochemical methods, no solubilization or purification of proteins is necessary for DCC-SMLM as it works with proteins in situ.
source: Unlike for biochemical methods, no solubilization or purification of proteins is necessary as DCC-SMLM works with proteins in situ.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage in the Discussion section.

claim: DCC-SMLM can be applied reliably even in small mammalian cells where the high densities of protein expression are usually problematic for photobleaching experiments.
source: In comparison to photobleaching experiments, DCC-SMLM can be applied reliably even in small mammalian cells where the high densities of protein expression are usually problematic.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage in the Discussion section.

claim: DCC-SMLM simplifies the procedure and offers greater reliability of counting compared to previously reported quantitative SMLM methods.
source: In contrast to previously reported quantitative SMLM methods, DCC-SMLM simplifies the procedure and offers greater reliability of counting.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage in the Discussion section.

claim: Binomial SMLM counting strategies require clustering of signals in at least three dimensions (x, y, and time) to identify individual protein subunits.
source: Binomial SMLM counting strategies require clustering of signals in at least three dimensions (x, y, and time) to identify individual protein subunits.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of existing methods in the Discussion section.

claim: DCC-SMLM only relies on the relationship between the total detection probability for a protein complex and the number of fluorophores within the complex, which is independent of temporal separation or demanding fluorophore properties.
source: In contrast, DCC-SMLM only relies on the relationship between the total detection probability for a protein complex and the number of fluorophores within the complex, as displayed in Equations 1 and 4. This relationship is independent of temporal separation or demanding fluorophore properties, such as high recall rates, thereby simplifying the data acquisition and post-processing.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage in the Discussion section.

claim: At the single molecule level, noise and genuine signals become hard to distinguish, especially for photoactivatable fluorescent proteins with low brightness such as PAmCherry.
source: At the single molecule level, noise and genuine signals become hard to distinguish, especially for photoactivatable fluorescent proteins with low brightness such as PAmCherry (Subach et al., 2009b).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Subach et al., 2009b.

claim: The measured background signal density in the PAmCherry channel of ~0.8 clusters/µm² inside cells suggests that only 2.6% of all mVenus molecules erroneously colocalize with the background clusters from the red channel.
source: Our measured background signal density in the PAmCherry channel of ~0.8 clusters/µm² inside cells (Figure 1E) suggests that only 2.6% of all mVenus molecules erroneously colocalize with the background clusters from the red channel (Equation 6).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on calculations from measured data.

claim: Given the colocalization ratios greater than 0.2 (for dimers and higher oligomeric forms), the background noise level results in a signal-to-noise ratio greater than 10.
source: Given the colocalization ratios greater than 0.2 (for dimers and higher oligomeric forms; Figure 4), this noise level results in a signal-to-noise ratio greater than 10.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on calculations.

claim: The use of the bright mVenus tag as the marker allowed for a narrow detection window, resulting in very low levels of background noise.
source: Our use of the bright mVenus tag as the marker allowed us to use a narrow detection window, resulting in very low levels of background noise (Figure 1D and Table 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by Figure 1D and Table 3.

claim: Fusion of two fluorescent proteins linked sequentially did not interfere with their structure as indicated by hrCNE results.
source: Fusion of two fluorescent proteins linked sequentially did not interfere with their structure as indicated by our hrCNE results (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Similar results for sequential fusion of fluorescent proteins have been reported previously for similar constructs in other contexts.
source: This may not be surprising as similar results have been reported previously for similar constructs in other contexts (Leeman et al., 2018; Liang et al., 2018; Murata et al., 2005; Ranade et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: DCC-SMLM can optimally distinguish oligomeric states from monomer to pentamer if p is between 0.2 and 0.4.
source: Theoretically, DCC-SMLM can optimally distinguish oligomeric states from monomer to pentamer if p is between 0.2 and 0.4 (Figure 1C; Figure 1—figure supplement 1), dependent on the oligomeric state of interest.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The original DCC model (Equations 1–3) suggested a recall rate of only 0.12 for PAmCherry.
source: The original DCC model (Equations 1–3) suggested a recall rate of only 0.12 for PAmCherry, but did not result in an optimal fit for our experimental data from reference proteins (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by Figure 4A.

claim: The modified DCC model with modification factor m suggested a slightly higher recall rate of 0.17 for PAmCherry and aligned well with the experimental data.
source: Fitting this modified DCC model to our reference data suggested a slightly higher recall rate of 0.17 for PAmCherry, and aligned well with the experimental data (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by Figure 4A.

claim: Previously reported recall rates for PAmCherry range from 0.04 when expressed in Escherichia coli to about 0.5 in Xenopus oocytes.
source: Previously reported recall rates for PAmCherry range from 0.04 when expressed in Escherichia coli (Wang et al., 2014) to about 0.5 in Xenopus oocytes (Durisic et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Wang et al., 2014 and Durisic et al., 2014.

claim: The variability in recall rates implies that the expression system may influence the functionality of fluorescent proteins.
source: This variability implies that the expression system may influence the functionality of fluorescent proteins.
evidence: This is stated as an inference in the Discussion section.

claim: The most likely cause for simultaneous loss of both fluorescent proteins is truncation within or proximal to mVenus.
source: Based on our experience with fluorescent protein-linked proteins, we assume that the most likely cause for such behavior is truncation within or proximal to mVenus.
evidence: This is stated as an assumption based on experience in the Discussion section.

claim: If the interest is only in determining higher oligomeric states (larger than dimers), the factor m may be omitted.
source: If the interest is only in determining higher oligomeric states (larger than dimers), the factor m may be omitted.
evidence: This is stated as a recommendation in the Discussion section.

claim: The determination of a monomeric state becomes almost impossible without m when taking the uncertainty of all values into account.
source: However, as theoretically expected, the determination of a monomeric state becomes almost impossible without m (Figure 4C–H) when taking the uncertainty of all values into account.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by Figure 4C-H.

claim: DCC-SMLM does not consider the behavior of individual protein complexes; instead, it is based on statistical information from a large number of protein complexes.
source: It should be emphasized that DCC-SMLM does not consider the behavior of individual protein complexes; instead, it is based on statistical information from a large number of protein complexes.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation in the Discussion section.

claim: If the protein complex of interest does not exist in a single oligomeric state, DCC-SMLM counting can only report an average oligomeric state.
source: Therefore, if the protein complex of interest does not exist in a single oligomeric state, DCC-SMLM counting can only report an average oligomeric state (simulated in Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated as a limitation in the Discussion section and supported by Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: A plot of the colocalization ratio versus the density of expressed clusters did not reveal any significant correlation between the two values, effectively ruling out aggregation over the expression densities achieved in the samples.
source: A plot of the colocalization ratio versus the density of expressed clusters (Figure 4—figure supplement 5) did not reveal any significant correlation between the two values, effectively ruling out aggregation over the expression densities achieved in our samples.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by Figure 4—figure supplement 5.

claim: Studies using Blue native electrophoresis previously reported a dimeric assembly for SLC26.
source: Studies using Blue native electrophoresis (Detro-Dassen et al., 2008) and X-ray and cryo-EM (Geertsma et al., 2015; Walter et al., 2019) previously reported a dimeric assembly for SLC26
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: X-ray and cryo-EM studies previously reported a dimeric assembly for SLC26.
source: Studies using Blue native electrophoresis (Detro-Dassen et al., 2008) and X-ray and cryo-EM (Geertsma et al., 2015; Walter et al., 2019) previously reported a dimeric assembly for SLC26
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: Microscopy approaches supported a tetrameric assembly for SLC26.
source: whereas microscopy approaches supported a tetrameric assembly (Hallworth and Nichols, 2012; Sinha et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: The discrepancy in SLC26 oligomeric state might indicate that SLC26 forms stable dimers that survive protein purification and solubilization as well as weakly associated 'dimer-of-dimer' tetramers in native membranes that may only be visible in intact cells.
source: This discrepancy might indicate that SLC26 forms stable dimers that survive protein purification and solubilization as well as weakly associated 'dimer-of-dimer' tetramers in native membranes that may only be visible in intact cells.
evidence: This is stated as a possible explanation in the Discussion section.

claim: Both prestin and SLC26A3 predominantly form dimers in intact HEK293T cells.
source: Although we cannot exclude the possibility that a minor fraction of prestin forms tetrameric structures, our results show that both prestin and SLC26A3 predominantly form dimers in intact HEK293T cells (Figure 4B–D).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by Figure 4B-D.

claim: vGlut1, -2, and -3 (Slc17a7, Slc17a6, and Slc17a8, respectively), and sialin (SLC17A5) are likely to be monomeric.
source: We also studied the oligomeric state of vGlut1, -2, and -3 (Slc17a7, Slc17a6, and Slc17a8, respectively), and sialin (SLC17A5) and found that they are likely to be monomeric.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the experimental results.

claim: The results for SLC17 proteins are consistent with native gel electrophoresis.
source: Again, these results are consistent with native gel electrophoresis (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Functional expression studies have demonstrated that vesicular glutamate transporters and sialin can function without accessory subunits.
source: Functional expression studies have also demonstrated that vesicular glutamate transporters and sialin can function without accessory subunits (Eriksen et al., 2016; Morin et al., 2004)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Eriksen et al., 2016 and Morin et al., 2004.

claim: SLC17 proteins are functional monomers.
source: which, when considered alongside our results, confirms that SLC17 proteins are functional monomers.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Discussion section based on multiple lines of evidence.

claim: The DCC principle is not reliant on SMLM and the algorithm may also be used with other microscopy modalities given enough spatial resolution to separate individual protein complexes.
source: In fact, while we use the x- and y-coordinates provided by SMLM, the DCC principle is not reliant on SMLM and the algorithm may also be used with other microscopy modalities given enough spatial resolution to separate individual protein complexes.
evidence: This is stated as a potential extension in the Discussion section.

claim: Examples of other microscopy modalities that could potentially use DCC include structured illumination and super-resolution radial fluctuations.
source: Examples may include structured illumination (Kner et al., 2009) and super-resolution radial fluctuations (Gustafsson et al., 2016) which are otherwise difficult to quantify at the single molecule level because they rely on the mathematical processing of multiple raw images to yield super-resolution images removing much of the information required by other algorithms.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kner et al., 2009 and Gustafsson et al., 2016.
